tier_reason: The page's -O2 table shows yxml at 1.15s (Wiki) and 0.74s (Discogs), against libxml2 2.9.1 at 2.53s/1.75s and Expat 2.1.0 at 1.47s/1.09s. The benchmark code is public in bench/ of g.blicky.net/yxml.git (Makefile, bench.c, runbench.sh), and it builds and runs libxml2, Expat and Mini-XML. The page states gcc 4.8.1 -O2, and the Makefile sets CFLAGS=-static -O2 with the musl-cross 0.9.13 toolchain. The page also states the CPU (3 GHz Intel E8400) and the OS (Linux 3.10.7).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 4.8.1 (musl-cross x86_64-linux-musl 0.9.13 toolchain, static linking), -static -O2; a second table uses -Os
corrections.hardware: Linux 3.10.7, 3 GHz Intel E8400 (the page says 'Core Duo'; the E8400 is a Core 2 Duo part), 4GB RAM
corrections.stars_or_usage: Self-hosted cgit, so no star count. The project page lists users including FreeBSD pkg, getdns, Fuchsia (SVG parsing), ncdc, BTstack, RetroArch, radare2 and Crank Storyboard. Unofficial GitHub copies exist (e.g. JulStrat/yxml, 13 stars; getdnsapi/yxml).
corrections.caveats: The benchmark dates from about 2013-2014 and ran on a 2008-era CPU (E8400) with 2013 library versions (libxml2 2.9.1, Expat 2.1.0). It is not compared against pugixml or RapidXML; the only rivals are Expat, libxml2 and Mini-XML. The numbers are the author's own, from his project page, and nobody has reproduced them independently. The comparison is not like-for-like: libxml2 runs through the xmlTextReader pull API with most features configured out (--without-push/sax1/tree/valid...), and Expat runs with no callbacks. yxml is non-validating, with no DTD or custom-entity support, so it does less work. Each timing is a single `time` of the whole process, including loading a pre-cached file. At -Os yxml is slower than Expat on the Wiki file (1.67s vs 1.58s) and faster on Discogs (1.02s vs 1.20s), though it still beats libxml2 (3.01s/2.08s). The repo is self-hosted cgit (unofficial GitHub copies exist) and has had no commits since 2020-11-08.

notes: The claimed numbers and the derived ratios (about 2.2x and 2.36x over libxml2, about 1.28x and 1.47x over Expat at -O2) match the page exactly. The license is MIT per the COPYING file, the last commit is 2020-11-08 per the cgit log, and the project is abandoned (more than 3 years old). The corrections only refine the toolchain and hardware wording, add usage details, and extend the caveats with how the benchmark was run and the -Os result.
